doc.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Organizing the Goodman concert and bringing in Teddy Wilson for the trio
summary: A union benefit concert sold out and made Time's cover; she then had Benny bring Teddy Wilson to form the first public interracial trio.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: It was a concert that Stanley and I had heard. Except the thing was not known in the U.S. you know. And so I went up to talk to Benny, and he’d had a very hard head you know, and only money talked to Benny. And so he listened you know, and he pulled a long face. And I said, “We’re going to put on a concert on Sunday with you.” And he’s thinking you know, what’s the money. And I said, “It’s a benefit for the union, and the union has agreed.” And so well he couldn’t really argue about that. So it was all set. And so what we did was, we gave a concert with the band, all these debbies were out selling all the tickets and it was absolutely sold out. And of course and Time magazine put it on the cover. This was a first. A concert of jazz, and these people. And so the follow-up on that was important, because I said to Benny, I want Teddy. And he said, “Who’s going to do it?” And I said, “You.” We’ll pay the fare to bring him. Well then I talked to Teddy and his wife Irene Wilson, you know, who wrote “Some Other Spring” and those things. She was a wonderful pianist, a woman pianist in Chicago in the early, early days. And so we brought Teddy, and we said well what we’ll do, Irving Kauffman was in charge of the house, and I said well what we’ll do is, there’s no dancing, it’s a concert. There’s no dance floor. So we’ll clear a little bit of the floor and we’ll bring Gene Krupa and Benny and Teddy down and the piano. And we’ll put on the trio. And that was the first time that inter-racial anything was ever given in public. And it was the Benny Goodman Trio. And so from there on of course Teddy stayed with the band and it all happened. So that was good.
That is — I didn’t know that that had happened like that.
